name: Feeling-the-Air Technique
description: Allows a Dragon-Blooded to sense her surroundings through minute eddies and currents in the air. She may move and act in total darkness or with vision fully impaired at no penalty, though she cannot read, tell colors, or discern anything that requires vision rather than spatial awareness. The sense is not precise enough to be completely effective in combat, but it reduces the penalties for fighting blind by half.

name: Soundless Action Prana
description: Eliminates the noise of any action taken directly by the character. Gravel crunches silently underfoot; a swung sword glances off a shield without sound. The effect lasts one minute per mote of Essence invested. It gives no direct bonus to Stealth rolls, but many actions no longer risk attracting attention. The suppression applies only to actions directly taken by the Dynast: she can put her fist through a window silently, but the falling glass tinkles, and a rock she throws crashes audibly. The character cannot speak while it is in effect but may communicate by any other method.

name: Zone of Silence Stance
duration: One minute per point of permanent Essence
description: By stilling the air so it ceases to transmit sound, an Air-aspected Exalt ensures the sounds of whatever mayhem ensues will not reach others. A Zone of Silence suppresses all sound within its reach — ringing blades, the cries of wounded enemies. No normal sound communication can take place within it, so the character should say anything needed before invoking it (Dynasts favoring it learn sign language or a Charm such as With One Mind). The Zone extends a number of yards equal to twice permanent Essence; each extra mote invested adds a yard of radius, but she cannot spend more motes to increase the area than her permanent Essence. The Zone moves with the character.

name: Distracting Breeze Meditation
description: The character uses the wind to cause minor disturbances — a tickling wind in the ear, a suddenly guttering torch, a knocked-over spear — that distract those who might observe her passage. Every mote of Essence invested acts as 2 automatic successes against a single target that might detect the Exalt's presence, and the Charm may be directed at more than one target at once so long as the Essence is paid. The character must not be visible or easily detectable when it is activated, though even a moment out of sight suffices to invoke it. It does nothing to conceal her passage (she may still be tracked). A character cannot spend more motes on this Charm than her permanent Essence.

name: Trackless Passage Style
description: Summons subtle air currents that conceal the traces of the passage of the character and her associates — obscuring footprints, obliterating scents, sweeping away broken branches and twigs. Every two motes invested completely obliterate all traces of one being's passage for a distance of one mile, including scent. Non-supernatural tracking fails automatically; supernatural tracking is subject to a standard tracking contest. The invoker may extend it to protect as many beings as he has points of permanent Essence.

name: Wind-Walking Technique
description: The character gains the ability to move normally along any roughly horizontal surface, even those normally impossible to cross — mud, quicksand, even water. It also instills perfect balance and timing, letting her scamper across ropes, poles, beams, and scaffolding with no movement penalty. She may move in all respects (jumping, rolling, crawling), but must keep moving: if even a single turn is spent standing still, the magic breaks. She can carry her normal gear and up to her own weight in extra burdens; any more immediately breaks the Charm.

name: Dragon Shroud Technique
description: Wraps the air itself around the character, concealing her even in broad daylight. She is not truly invisible, but her form is blurred and indistinct as light bends around her, making her very hard to see even when the observer knows she is there and nearly impossible when he does not. The shroud also muffles sound, masks scent, and suppresses body heat. A careful or lucky observer can still spot a blurry disturbance in the air. Every 3 motes invested act as one automatic opposing success against any action taken against her that requires she be seen, heard, or perceived with any of the five senses (including attacks and attempts to spot her sneaking), and it masks her identity. It has no lingering effect; she can be tracked as normal.
